title: District of Columbia Courts, Public Defender Service, and Court Services and Offender Supervision Agency Act of 2015
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the Senate reported version is repeated here.)

District of Columbia Courts, Public Defender Service, and Court Services and Offender Supervision Agency Act of 2015

(Sec. 2) Amends the District of Columbia Code to authorize the Executive Officer of the District of Columbia courts to:

  • collect debts owed to the District of Columbia courts because of erroneous payments made to current and former court employees, or any other debt; and
  • purchase uniforms to be worn by certain nonjudicial employees of the District courts, so long as the cost of furnishing a uniform during a year does not exceed the amount applicable to the uniform allowance for federal employees.

(Sec. 3) Amends the National Capital Revitalization and Self-Government Improvement Act of 1997 to authorize the Director of the Court Services and Offender Supervision Agency to develop and operate intermediate incentive programs for sentenced offenders.

Makes permanent the Director's authority to accept, solicit, and use on behalf of the Agency: (1) any monetary or nonmonetary gift, donation, bequest, or use of facilities, property, or services to aid or facilitate the work of the Agency; and (2) reimbursements from the District government for space and services provided, on a cost reimbursable basis.

(Sec. 4) Amends the District of Columbia Court Reform and Criminal Procedure Act of 1970 to:

  • authorize the Public Defender Service, upon approval of the Board of Trustees, to accept (as currently allowed) and use public grants, private contributions, and voluntary and uncompensated (gratuitous) services to assist it; and
  • deem members of the Board of Trustees, as of October 21, 1998, to be employees of the Service instead of District employees for purposes of any action brought against them.

summary.headline: This law makes several administrative changes to how the District of Columbia's courts, public defender office, and offender supervision agency handle money, staff, and programs.
summary.what_it_does: It lets the court system's executive officer collect money owed to the courts, such as erroneous payments to current or former employees, and buy uniforms for certain nonjudicial court workers within the federal uniform allowance limit. It lets the Court Services and Offender Supervision Agency create intermediate incentive programs for sentenced offenders and permanently accept gifts and reimbursements from the District government. It also lets the Public Defender Service accept grants, private contributions, and free services with board approval, and treats certain 1998 Board of Trustees members as Service employees in lawsuits.

who_it_affects.group: Current and former employees of the D.C. courts
who_it_affects.how: The court system can seek repayment of money it paid them by mistake.
The court system can buy uniforms for them, as long as yearly costs stay within the federal uniform allowance amount.

who_it_affects.group: Sentenced offenders in D.C. supervised by the Court Services and Offender Supervision Agency
who_it_affects.how: The agency can create and run intermediate incentive programs that may apply to them.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the Public Defender Service Board of Trustees as of October 21, 1998
who_it_affects.how: They are treated as Public Defender Service employees, rather than District employees, in lawsuits brought against them.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 28, 2016; the summary does not list a separate effective date.
